News Items 
 
Risk Management 
The latest quarterly review of the Corporate Risk Register by Management Team 
took place in September 2025, with the document updated for actions arising from 
the exercise. The next Management Team review of the Corporate Risk Register is 
scheduled for 09 December 2025 (see page 20). 
 
Osberstown Cottage – New Transitional Housing for Women 
Kildare County Council has officially opened Osberstown Cottage, a new shared 
transitional housing service. This facility will provide secure, short-term 
accommodation for up to five women experiencing homelessness or at risk of 
homelessness, (see page 21-22). 
 
Community Support Centres (CSCs) 
Following the receipt of guidance from Government regarding emergency planning, 
the Council is conducting a process to designate locations across Municipal Districts, 
as Community Support Centres (see pages 49-50). 
 
Climate Action - Demo House 
Visits to the Council’s DemoHouse continue to be popular with many seeking 
information on energy retrofits.  The awards from SEAI and Entente Florale are 
aiding interest alongside word of mouth (see page 54). 
 
Local Enterprise Office - K-Hub Award 
The Council’s K-Hub Strategy was shortlisted in the Chambers Ireland Excellence in 
Local Government Awards 2025, and on 27 November was named the winner in the 
Promoting Economic Development Category.(see page 79).

Housing Delivery  
Information has been published on the Council’s website launching a competitive 
dialogue procurement process for the delivery of new housing schemes across the 
county as part of our housing delivery programme.  The tender was published on 
eTenders on 19 November, with final submissions required by 19 December.  It is 
expected that the initial assessment of the tenders will commence in January (see 
pages 20-21). 
 
Local Community Safety Partnership 
Local Community Safety Partnerships (LCSPs) are multi-agency bodies established 
under the Policing, Security and Community Safety Act 2024. Work is underway on 
the formation of the Kildare LCSP. The deadline for a youth representative and 
Kildare - Newbridge Municipal District representative, has been extended until 
5.00p.m. on Tuesday 09 December (see page 45). 
 
Veterinary Services 
The ISPCA will no longer provide the Dog Warden Service for Kildare County 
Council after 31 December, 2025.  The service was tendered and a contract with the 
preferred bidder is nearing finalisation.  The new service provider will commence 
operations in early January (see page 62). 
 
Into Kildare 
Áine Mangan took part in a pre-recorded segment with Virgin Media in Kildare 
Village, which will be broadcast on the 08 December, with a key focus on tourism in 
County Kildare. The report highlighted the county’s strengths as a visitor destination. 
The lifestyle offering on the segment will support the continued promotion of Kildare 
to a national audience (see pages 78-79).

Kildare County Council is proud to 
launch the new Irish language initiative 
Scéim na bhFáinní through which we 
celebrate our rich Irish language 
heritage and empower sixth class 
students to embrace spoken Irish in 
their daily lives.  
Coiste Gaeilge has built upon the pilot 
scheme and research done by the 
outgoing Coiste Gaeilge committee, 
and are delighted to now administer 
Scéim na bhFáinní to up to 20 schools 
across County Kildare.  The scheme 
will be implemented this school year 
with support from Cill Dara le Gaeilge 
and Conradh na Gaeilge.  
Content and Language Integrated 
Learning (CLIL) is central to the 
programme e.g. Ealaín (Art) through 
Irish, Corpoideachas (Physical 
Education) through Irish, Ceol (Music) 
through Irish etc. Students will also 
undertake two Irish language-related 
projects of their own choosing.   
The Irish language seanfhocal 
(proverb) “Mol an Óige agus Tiocfaidh 
Sí” encourages the celebration of 
children’s achievements as a way in 
which confidence is fostered.  
Members of Coiste Gaeilge believe 
this seanfhocal aptly encapsulates the 
ethos and objective of Scéim na 
bhFáinní.

As Members are aware, the budget in the public sector represents the ceiling to 
funding provision of a service – i.e. excluding additional grants, the budget amount is 
the maximum spend that can be incurred.  
Estimates are fixed and service delivery is limited to within the envelope of funding.  
If a budget holder wants/needs to increase some aspect of the service beyond the 
budget provision, they need to source the funding elsewhere by reducing some other 
line of expenditure or by receiving additional grant income. You will note that the 
expenditure and income in Housing and Building is significantly ahead of budget this 
is due to additional expenditure and matching increased income on social housing 
leasing initiatives.

newcomers’ sense of belonging and 
fosters social cohesion, while 
demonstrating how national funding 
can be used strategically to enhance 
local capacity and ensure that local 
integration is both immediate and 
sustainable.

local government can drive sustainable
